pairs: Fugit impius nemine persequente;
The impious flees, though no one pursues.
justus autem,
But the just,
quasi leo confidens,
like a confident lion,
absque terrore erit.
shall be without dread.
Propter peccata terræ multi principes ejus;
Because of the sins of the land, it has many princes.
et propter hominis sapientiam,
And because of the wisdom of a man,
et horum scientiam quæ dicuntur,
and the knowledge of those things that are said,
vita ducis longior erit.
the life of the leader shall be prolonged.
Vir pauper calumnians pauperes similis est imbri vehementi in quo paratur fames.
A poor man slandering the poor is like a violent rainstorm in advance of a famine.
Qui derelinquunt legem laudant impium;
Those who abandon the law praise the impious.
qui custodiunt, succenduntur contra eum.
Those who guard it are inflamed against him.
Viri mali non cogitant judicium;
Evil men do not intend judgment.
qui autem inquirunt Dominum animadvertunt omnia.
But those who inquire after the Lord turn their souls toward all things.
Melior est pauper ambulans in simplicitate sua quam dives in pravis itineribus.
Better is the pauper walking in his simplicity, than the rich walking in ways of depravity.
Qui custodit legem filius sapiens est;
Whoever keeps the law is a wise son.
qui autem comessatores pascit confundit patrem suum.
But whoever feeds gluttons brings shame to his father.
Qui coacervat divitias usuris et fœnore,
Whoever piles up riches by usury
liberali in pauperes congregat eas.
and profit gathers them for him who will give freely to the poor.
Qui declinat aures suas ne audiat legem,
Whoever turns away his ears from listening to the law:
oratio ejus erit execrabilis.
his prayer will be detestable.
Qui decipit justos in via mala, in interitu suo corruet,
Whoever deceives the just in a malicious way will fall into his own perdition.
et simplices possidebunt bona ejus.
And the simple shall possess his goods.
Sapiens sibi videtur vir dives;
The rich one seems wise to himself.
pauper autem prudens scrutabitur eum.
But the poor one, being prudent, shall evaluate him.
In exsultatione justorum multa gloria est;
In the exultation of the just, there is great glory.
regnantibus impiis,
When the impious reign,
ruinæ hominum.
men are brought to ruin.
Qui abscondit scelera sua non dirigetur;
Whoever hides his crimes will not be guided.
qui autem confessus fuerit et reliquerit ea,
But whoever will have confessed
misericordiam consequetur.
and abandoned them shall overtake mercy.
Beatus homo qui semper est pavidus;
Blessed is the man who is ever fearful. Yet truly,
qui vero mentis est duræ corruet in malum.
whoever is hardened in mind will fall into evil.
Leo rugiens et ursus esuriens,
An impious leader over a poor people is like a roaring lion
princeps impius super populum pauperem.
and a hungry bear.
Dux indigens prudentia multos opprimet per calumniam;
A leader destitute of prudence will oppress many through false accusations.
qui autem odit avaritiam, longi fient dies ejus.
But whoever hates avarice shall prolong his days.
Hominem qui calumniatur animæ sanguinem,
A man who slanders the blood of a life,
si usque ad lacum fugerit,
even if he flees to the pit,
nemo sustinet.
no one will tolerate him.
Qui ambulat simpliciter salvus erit;
Whoever walks simply shall be saved.
qui perversis graditur viis concidet semel.
Whoever is perverse in his steps will fall all at once.
Qui operatur terram suam satiabitur panibus;
Whoever works his land shall be satisfied with bread.
qui autem sectatur otium replebitur egestate.
But whoever pursues leisure will be filled with need.
Vir fidelis multum laudabitur;
A faithful man shall be greatly praised.
qui autem festinat ditari non erit innocens.
But whoever rushes to become rich will not be innocent.
Qui cognoscit in judicio faciem non bene facit;
Whoever shows favoritism in judgment does not do well;
iste
even if it is for a morsel of bread,
et pro buccella panis deserit veritatem.
he forsakes the truth.
Vir qui festinat ditari,
A man who hurries to become rich,
et aliis invidet,
and who envies others,
ignorat quod egestas superveniet ei.
does not know that destitution will overwhelm him.
Qui corripit hominem gratiam postea inveniet apud eum,
Whoever corrects a man, afterward he shall find favor with him,
magis quam ille qui per linguæ blandimenta decipit.
more so than he who deceives him with a flattering tongue.
Qui subtrahit aliquid a patre suo
Whoever takes away anything from his father or mother,
et a matre,
and who says,
et dicit hoc non esse peccatum,
“This is not a sin,”
particeps homicidæ est.
is the associate of a murderer.
Qui se jactat et dilatat,
Whoever boasts and enlarges himself stirs up conflicts.
jurgia concitat;
Yet truly,
qui vero sperat in Domino sanabitur.
whoever trusts in the Lord will be healed.
Qui confidit in corde suo stultus est;
Whoever trusts in his own heart is a fool.
qui autem graditur sapienter,
But whoever treads wisely,
ipse salvabitur.
the same shall be saved.
Qui dat pauperi non indigebit;
Whoever gives to the poor shall not be in need.
qui despicit deprecantem sustinebit penuriam.
Whoever despises his petition will suffer scarcity.
Cum surrexerint impii,
When the impious rise up,
abscondentur homines;
men will hide themselves.
cum illi perierint,
When they perish,
multiplicabuntur justi.
the just shall be multiplied.
